questions.q: What is activation patching, in general terms?
options: Permanently editing a model's weights to fix an error
Running a model on two related inputs and splicing an activation from one run into the corresponding position of the other run's forward pass, then observing the effect on output
Training a sparse autoencoder on a model's activations
Visualizing attention weights as a heatmap with no intervention on the model
questions.explain: Activation patching is a causal intervention: swap one activation between two paired runs and see what changes, isolating that activation's causal role.

questions.q: What is the procedure behind causal tracing, as used in Meng et al.'s ROME paper?
options: Train a probe on frozen activations and read off its accuracy

Corrupt a factual prompt's subject tokens with noise, then selectively restore one component's clean activation at a time (sweeping layers and positions) and measure how much correct-answer probability returns
Delete the model's MLP layers entirely and compare outputs
Fine-tune the whole model on a dataset of similar facts
questions.explain: Causal tracing sweeps restoration patches across every (layer, position) pair after corrupting the subject tokens, producing a localization heatmap.

questions.q: What was the central finding of the causal-tracing experiments in "Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT"?
options: Factual recall is spread evenly across every layer of the model with no localization
Factual recall is concentrated in middle-layer MLP modules, specifically at the subject token's last position
Factual recall occurs exclusively in the model's embedding layer
Factual recall cannot be localized by any causal method
questions.explain: The paper found a surprisingly localized result -- middle-layer MLPs at the subject's last token position -- which directly motivated the ROME editing method.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish activation patching from the probing classifiers covered in Chapter 5?
options: They are described as identical methods with different names
Probing asks a correlational question (does a direction correlate with a property); patching asks a causal question (does intervening on this activation actually change the model's behavior)
Probing is a causal method and patching is correlational -- the reverse of what's stated
Neither method involves looking at a model's internal activations
questions.explain: A probe finding a correlated direction doesn't prove the model's forward computation uses it; patching tests that directly by intervening and observing the causal effect.

questions.q: In the lesson's `causal_trace` code, what does a brighter cell in the resulting `results` heatmap indicate?
options: That patching in the clean activation at that specific layer and position restored more of the correct answer's probability, marking it as more causally important to the fact
That the model's loss increased at that layer
That more parameters exist at that layer than at others
That the corrupted run and clean run produced identical outputs everywhere
questions.explain: Each cell measures how much correct-answer probability comes back when just that one (layer, position) pair's clean activation is restored -- brighter cells mark where the fact's information is most concentrated.
